incidents.victim: Instructure (Canvas) — 9,000 universities & K-12 schools
incidents.vector: Voice phishing of employee Okta SSO credentials; attackers exploited a Free-For-Teacher account issue to maintain access after initial containment, then defaced the Canvas login page with a ransom demand.
incidents.impact: Canvas platform taken fully offline during final exams week, disrupting Baylor, Penn, Duke, Princeton, Ohio State and dozens of other universities; ShinyHunters claims 3.6 TB of data including names, emails, student IDs and messages on 275M students and faculty.

incidents.victim: Ivanti Endpoint Manager Mobile (EPMM) customers
incidents.vector: Improper input validation vulnerability (CVE-2026-6973) in Ivanti EPMM under active exploitation; CISA added it to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog.
incidents.impact: Federal Civilian Executive Branch agencies ordered to remediate; affects organizations worldwide using Ivanti EPMM for mobile device management.

incidents.victim: Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS firewall customers
incidents.vector: Buffer-overflow zero-day (CVE-2026-0300, CVSS 9.3) in PAN-OS User-ID Authentication Portal; unauthenticated RCE on PA-Series and VM-Series firewalls. Attackers injected shellcode into nginx, deployed EarthWorm and ReverseSocks5 tunnels, and used firewall service-account credentials for Active Directory enumeration.
incidents.impact: Patches not yet available (expected May 13); CISA ordered federal agencies to apply mitigations immediately. Over 5,800 publicly exposed VM-Series firewalls identified. Unit 42 tracks the activity as CL-STA-1132 — a likely state-sponsored cluster.

incidents.victim: Carnival cruise customers (7.5 million)
incidents.vector: Personal data stolen in an earlier 2026 ShinyHunters intrusion was published online this week. The same campaign also hit Zara, 7-Eleven, Udemy and Medtronic.
incidents.impact: 7.5 million customer records leaked publicly; high risk of follow-on phishing and identity-theft scams.

incidents.victim: Microsoft customers — SharePoint and Windows Defender
incidents.vector: Microsoft May 2026 Patch Tuesday fixed 167 vulnerabilities, including an actively-exploited SharePoint Server spoofing zero-day (CVE-2026-32201) and a publicly-disclosed Windows Defender privilege-escalation bug dubbed 'BlueHammer' (CVE-2026-33825).
incidents.impact: SharePoint flaw enables spoofing of trusted content to fuel phishing, data manipulation and social-engineering against employees, partners and customers; defenders urged to patch immediately.

incidents.victim: Trellix (cybersecurity vendor)
incidents.vector: Unauthorized access to a portion of Trellix's source code repository; the company has not disclosed how the breach occurred.
incidents.impact: Trellix says no evidence its source-code release or distribution process was affected or that source code was exploited; raises supply-chain concerns for downstream customers since source code can reveal where security controls and detections are implemented.

incidents.victim: Government entities in South America and southeastern Europe
incidents.vector: China-nexus APT 'UAT-8302' deploys custom malware including NetDraft (a C# variant of FinalDraft/SquidDoor), an updated CloudSorcerer backdoor, VSHELL, the SNOWLIGHT stager and a new Rust-based SNOWRUST stager after initial access; uses Impacket and PowerShell for AD reconnaissance.
incidents.impact: Long-term access to government networks across multiple regions; shared tooling indicates a tight operational cluster with several other publicly known Chinese-speaking APTs.

incidents.victim: Unnamed enterprise (Phone Link OTP theft target)
incidents.vector: Attacker implants the CloudZ RAT (delivered via a fake ScreenConnect update and a Rust dropper that drops a .NET loader) plus a new 'Pheno' plugin that hijacks Microsoft Phone Link's PC-to-phone bridge to read SMS-based OTPs from the synced SQLite database.
incidents.impact: Allows interception of authenticator and SMS OTP messages without compromising the victim's phone; active since at least January 2026 and demonstrates a novel MFA-bypass technique.

incidents.victim: Linux server and Kubernetes operators (broad)
incidents.vector: 'Copy Fail' (CVE-2026-31431) — deterministic logic flaw in the Linux kernel's algif_aead crypto module allows any local unprivileged user to overwrite the page cache of setuid binaries (e.g. /usr/bin/su) and escalate to root using a 732-byte Python script. Works across Ubuntu, RHEL, SUSE, Amazon Linux, Debian and others (kernels 4.14-6.19.12).
incidents.impact: Enables container escape, multi-tenant compromise and CI/CD pipeline takeover. Added to the CISA KEV catalog; a fully working PoC is public and exploitation is expected to spread quickly.

incidents.victim: US Department of Defense — service member records (via Schemata)
incidents.vector: AI virtual-training platform Schemata, a DOD contractor, exposed US service member records and sensitive military training course data via an API left online without authentication. Researcher firm Strix reported the issue; Schemata took 150 days to secure it.
incidents.impact: Sensitive defense training material and personnel records exposed for an extended period to anyone with the API endpoint.

incidents.victim: Mediaworks (Hungarian pro-Orbán media conglomerate)
incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — data extortion (World Leaks / former Hunters International)
incidents.vector: Ransomware-style intrusion followed by data theft; World Leaks (a Hunters International rebrand focused on extortion without encryption) published nearly 8.5 TB of internal files on its dark-web leak site.
incidents.impact: Leak exposed payroll, contracts, financial statements and editorial communications — including a January 2025 memo suggesting Mediaworks would 'contact Moscow for help' coordinating anti-Zelensky coverage. Mediaworks threatened legal action against journalists who covered the leak.

incidents.victim: DigiCert
incidents.vector: Social-engineering attack tricked two DigiCert tech-support staff into running a malicious .SCR (Windows screensaver) file, masquerading as a customer. CrowdStrike EDR on one host was misconfigured and failed to alert, letting the attacker dwell for nearly two weeks and harvest 'initialization codes' for in-progress EV code-signing orders.
incidents.impact: 27 EV code-signing certificates issued to customer accounts and used to sign Zhong Stealer malware (previously associated with a Chinese e-crime group); all 60 affected orders revoked.

incidents.victim: Targeted government, scientific, manufacturing and retail orgs in Russia, Belarus and Thailand
incidents.vector: Supply-chain compromise of DAEMON Tools (AVB Disc Soft); installers signed with the vendor's legitimate certificate have shipped a fingerprinting backdoor since at least April 8 that selectively deploys the QUIC RAT on high-value hosts.
incidents.impact: Several thousand infections worldwide, but the second-stage QUIC RAT was deployed on only about a dozen carefully selected systems — the same targeted operational pattern Chinese APTs used in past Notepad++ and CCleaner compromises.

incidents.victim: Indian and Russian organizations (industrial, consulting, retail, transportation)
incidents.vector: Chinese threat actor 'Silver Fox' sent 1,600+ tax-themed phishing emails impersonating Indian tax authorities (December) and then Russian tax authorities (January-February), delivering a Rust-based loader, ValleyRAT, and a previously undocumented Python backdoor ('ABCDoor') that uses HTTPS/Socket.IO C2.
incidents.impact: Persistent remote access with multimonitor screen streaming, mouse/keyboard control, clipboard theft and file operations. Marks Silver Fox's first known expansion into Russian targets.

incidents.victim: Cuban Embassy in Washington, DC
incidents.vector: Compromise of a Microsoft Exchange email server at the Cuban embassy; the same actor breached more than 5,000 Exchange servers globally this year.
incidents.impact: Stolen diplomat email inboxes, reportedly used to spy on US naval blockade activity in the region.

incidents.victim: Moldova National Health Insurance Agency (CNAM)
incidents.vector: Unknown intrusion into Moldova's national healthcare database; no ransom demand was made. Moldovan officials did not exclude Russian involvement amid renewed Russian military threats against Moldova.
incidents.impact: Personal and financial data on nearly every adult Moldovan, plus financial details of private medical providers, were stolen or had to be restored from backup. CNAM said payments and medical services were unaffected.

incidents.victim: cPanel/WHM shared-hosting servers (~1.5M instances exposed online)
incidents.vector: Critical authentication-bypass (CVE-2026-41940, CVSS 9.8) in cPanel/WHM caused by improper handling of line breaks in login-form input, allowing arbitrary data injection into pre-auth session files. Exploitation began before the patch was issued.
incidents.impact: Shadowserver counted 44,000+ compromised cPanel systems; attackers used the bug for cryptominers, DDoS malware and a 'Fakestortion' campaign that wiped websites and posted $8,000 Bitcoin ransom notes. Several Guam government sites were taken offline. ACSC issued a critical alert; CISA added the CVE to the KEV.

incidents.victim: Brazilian internet service providers (small regional ISPs)
incidents.vector: An attacker who breached Brazilian DDoS-mitigation firm Huge Networks in January built a Mirai-based botnet from TP-Link Archer AX21 routers (CVE-2023-1389) and unmanaged DNS resolvers, then used Huge Networks's own infrastructure and the CEO's SSH keys to launch DNS-amplification DDoS attacks against small Brazilian ISPs.
incidents.impact: Multi-year DDoS campaign exposed in a leaked attacker archive; Huge Networks's CEO claims a competitor was sabotaging the company's reputation. The botnet attacked targets in 10-60 second bursts across Brazilian IP ranges.

incidents.victim: Organizations infected by TeamPCP supply-chain attacks (manufacturing, healthcare, education, tech)
incidents.vector: Vect 2.0 ransomware-as-a-service — launched as TeamPCP's affiliate to exploit downstream victims of recent Trivy/KICS/LiteLLM/Telnyx supply-chain compromises — has a ChaCha20 implementation flaw that discards 3 of 4 decryption nonces for any file over 128 KB, permanently destroying the bulk of large files (VM disks, DBs, backups).
incidents.impact: Functions as a wiper rather than a true ransomware: victims who pay receive a decryptor that cannot recover the bulk of their data because the encryption key material is irrecoverable.

incidents.victim: Five Polish water treatment facilities
incidents.vector: Five water treatment facilities across Poland were hacked last year; attackers gained access to industrial control systems at some of them. Poland's intelligence service (ABW) disclosed the incidents but did not attribute them.
incidents.impact: Disclosed scope: ICS access at multiple treatment plants — a concerning precedent for OT-targeting against European water infrastructure.

incidents.victim: US Federal Civilian Executive Branch agencies and 11 state/local governments
incidents.vector: Ongoing exploitation of two Cisco ASA zero-days (CVE-2025-20333 CVSS 9.9 and CVE-2025-20362) — VPN web service memory corruption chained for RCE and persistence across reboots and software upgrades on 5500-X Series appliances.
incidents.impact: CISA found that some agencies had patched to versions still vulnerable; attackers targeted 12 federal IPs and government IPs in India, Nigeria, Japan, the UK and 10+ other countries, plus US financial institutions, defense contractors and military orgs. Tied to last year's ArcaneDoor campaign.

incidents.victim: Retail and hospitality organizations (and healthcare, tech, transport, logistics)
incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — data extortion (BlackFile / Cordial Spider)
incidents.vector: Voice-phishing of help-desk staff to harvest single-sign-on credentials, followed by abuse of Microsoft Graph and Salesforce APIs, SharePoint and code-repo exfiltration. Some victims have been swatted to pressure ransom payment.
incidents.impact: Multi-industry data theft and seven-figure ransom demands; activity overlaps with the CrowdStrike-tracked 'Cordial Spider' campaign ongoing since October 2025.

incidents.victim: Cloud, container and developer infrastructure operators (broad)
incidents.vector: 'PCPJack' modular cloud worm scans for exposed cloud services, exfiltrates secrets from Gmail/Outlook, AWS, GitHub, Slack, Stripe, Coinbase, Binance and crypto wallets, then propagates by downloading Common Crawl parquet files for stealthy, pre-validated target discovery.
incidents.impact: Targets organizations already infected by rival TeamPCP and removes that malware before stealing cloud, container and crypto secrets. Spreading laterally via stolen Kubernetes/Docker/Redis/SSH credentials.

incidents.victim: Windows server and workstation users (broad)
incidents.vector: 'PhantomRPC' architectural flaw in Windows RPC allows a low-privileged process holding SeImpersonatePrivilege to register an RPC server that impersonates a missing legitimate service, hijacking calls from higher-privileged processes to escalate to SYSTEM.
incidents.impact: Microsoft rated the bug 'moderate' and declined to issue a patch or CVE. Kaspersky published PoCs covering five exploit paths; defenders must rely on Event Tracing for Windows monitoring and tighter SeImpersonatePrivilege scoping.
